name: Jralo for WooCommerce
author: gosu1210

sections.description:
Jralo helps you keep accessibility barriers, broken website experiences and security risks in view. This plugin brings your Jralo results into WordPress and WooCommerce, so you can see what needs attention and give your developer clear next steps.

  • Accessibility findings against WCAG 2.2 A and AA, organized by severity.
  • Website QA findings for broken experiences, with practical next steps.
  • Security findings, a score and a grade. Paid plans include the supporting evidence and fix steps.
  • Traffic, attack and bot alerts through your connected Jralo service.
  • A link to your full report and independently timestamped evidence in Jralo.
  • Website Mechanic fixes you can review before installing a changed theme.
  • An optional monitoring badge as a footer setting, block or shortcode.

The plugin works on WordPress sites with or without WooCommerce. When WooCommerce is active, it also provides store-specific guidance and links to important store pages.

Review your results in WordPress

See your latest accessibility, website QA and security results, including their dates. Start an available check from WordPress within your plan’s allowance, or open the full report in Jralo.

A free Jralo account includes checks for one site, up to three times a day, covering the homepage and up to five linked pages. Paid plans add ongoing monitoring and the features described on the pricing page. Current plans and optional add-ons: https://jralo.com/pricing/

Fixes you control

Request a Website Mechanic fix for your theme and download the changed theme for review. You choose whether to upload, preview and activate it through WordPress. The plugin does not install or activate a theme for you. Your first fix is free.

Show your monitoring badge

Choose whether to display the Monitored by Jralo badge. The footer setting is off until you turn it on. Badge access depends on your Jralo account features. Your public record has a separate switch and can remain private. A private record’s badge links to Jralo; a published record’s badge links to that record.

Use the block, footer setting or shortcode [jralo_badge]. Styles: dark, light, color and compact.

Important limits

Automated monitoring cannot find every problem or prevent every failure or attack. Pair it with manual tests of important customer journeys. A result is not a statement that your site meets a law or standard. This is not legal advice.

The plugin is not a firewall, malware remover or accessibility overlay. It does not place orders, change your cart or sign into your customer accounts. Your website’s security controls remain important.

External services

A Jralo account is required. The service is operated by Misimi Corp at https://jralo.com/.

Nothing is sent to Jralo until you enter a connection token and press Connect. Installing and activating the plugin makes no outside requests.

After you connect, the plugin communicates with Jralo to retrieve your results and badge status, carry out actions you request, provide security activity reporting on eligible plans, and remove the connection when you disconnect. Results refresh when you use the plugin and in the background while connected.

Requests include your connection token and the plugin’s name and version. Jralo also receives your server’s IP address. Security activity reporting includes activity counts and IP addresses associated with suspected abuse. It does not send passwords, form contents, customer records or orders.

Website Mechanic sends your active theme’s code, and parent-theme code for a child theme, only when you request a fix. This includes the theme’s name and version. It does not send images, database contents or settings. An AI processing provider handles that code for the requested fix. Submitted code is removed when the job finishes; changed theme files are retained for 30 days so you can download them.

Jralo sends back your connected site’s address, plan, result dates, counts and findings, with supporting evidence and fix steps where your plan includes them. The plugin stores these results and your connection token in your WordPress database.

If you display the badge, visitors’ browsers request its image from jralo.com. Jralo receives their IP address and browser type as part of that request. The badge sets no cookies and runs no script. Suggested privacy wording is available in WordPress under Settings > Privacy > Policy Guide.

The plugin contains no advertising analytics. Disconnecting removes the connection. Deleting the plugin removes its saved token, results, badge settings and background tasks.

  • Terms: https://jralo.com/terms/
  • Privacy: https://jralo.com/privacy/
  • Badge Terms: https://jralo.com/badge-terms/
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate the plugin.
  2. Open Jralo in your WordPress admin menu.
  3. In https://jralo.com/app/, add your site and create a connection token under “Connect a WordPress or WooCommerce site”.
  4. Paste the token into WordPress and press Connect.
  5. Press Check now, or review your latest available results.
  6. Optional: enable your badge in Jralo, then use its footer setting, block or shortcode in WordPress.
sections.faq:
Does this make my site accessible or legally compliant?

No. It gives you findings and next steps. Automated monitoring cannot find every problem, and no result is a legal determination. This is not legal advice.

Do I need WooCommerce?

No. The plugin also works on WordPress sites without WooCommerce.

Does the plugin cost anything?

The plugin is free. A Jralo account is required. Free and paid service features are listed at https://jralo.com/pricing/. Paid plans are purchased through Jralo, not inside the plugin.

Does it place orders or change my cart?

No. It does not place orders, change carts or sign into customer accounts.

Why is my badge not showing?

Check your badge access and settings in Jralo, then enable the WordPress footer setting, block or shortcode. A new site’s badge appears after its first successful check. Publishing your public record is a separate choice.

What if a check is still waiting?

Use Refresh to see the latest available result. A request that stops waiting does not necessarily mean the check failed.

How do I disconnect?

Press Disconnect in WordPress or remove the connection in your Jralo dashboard. The connection token cannot change your billing.

Can I use this for a private or local website?

The site must be reachable on the public internet for Jralo to check it.
